claims.text: The catalyst's enhanced ethanol-oxidation performance is governed by its distribution of crystal facets.
Surface oxidation states govern the catalyst's enhanced ethanol-oxidation performance.
Crystal facets and surface oxidation states modulate the binding energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The reported PGM nanoscale catalysts have mixed surface facets, including Pt(111) and Pt(100), and native surface oxidation states.
A controlled thermal or chemical treatment can enrich Pt(111)-like surface facets while tuning surface oxidation states.
Facet distribution and associated oxidation states directly influence adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Facet distribution and associated oxidation states directly influence ethanol-oxidation reaction pathways.
Modifying the catalyst surface structure alters its electronic properties.
Pt(111) facets optimally stabilize crucial ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Stabilization of crucial intermediates reduces over-oxidation.
Stabilization of crucial intermediates reduces catalyst poisoning.
Reduced over-oxidation and poisoning enhance catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability.
Facet-enriched catalysts with controlled surface oxidation states will show higher ethanol-oxidation activity than untreated catalysts.
Facet-enriched catalysts with controlled surface oxidation states will show higher product selectivity than untreated catalysts.
Facet-enriched catalysts with controlled surface oxidation states will resist poisoning or degradation better than untreated catalysts.
The proposed mechanism may fail at very low temperatures because they do not promote surface restructuring.
The proposed mechanism may fail at very high ethanol concentrations because active sites become overwhelmed.
Particle-size distribution and support interactions may also contribute to catalytic performance.
